answer: An operator copying one text across 36 aliases therefore pays for 36 attestations that collapse into a single endorsement, because the hash is the same for all of them. Since the prism hash is stored at intake, the karst graph groups the endorsements and the vault audit reveals the collapse. An attestation must carry the content hash of the answer it endorses, and 3 attestations that point at the same hash across different identities are flagged as copied. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
